# What the margins pay for

Cost of goods runs $133,931 a month against $517,177 of revenue, a blended 74.1% margin. What they cover:

| Category | Margin | What the cost side is |
|---|---|---|
| Recovery | 80–85% | Consumables, filters and water treatment, linens, device servicing contracts. Almost no per-session variable cost, which is why these margins are the highest in the building. |
| Regenerative | 72–78% | PRP kits and centrifuge consumables, IV bags, vitamins and NAD+, peptides and pharmacy cost, tubing and sharps. |
| Aesthetics | 65–70% | Neuromodulator and filler units at acquisition cost, laser tips and consumables, RF and cryo applicators, topicals. The lowest wellness margins because product cost dominates. |
| Diagnostics | 62–70% | Reference lab send-out fees, DEXA consumables, DNA and DUTCH collection kits, interpretation time. |
| Surgery — facility fee | 78–80% | Disposables, implants, drugs and linens, instrument reprocessing. Clinical staff sits in fixed overhead and the surgeon takes no share of the facility fee, which is why these exceed the treatment-room lines. |
| Surgery — full fee | 73–76% | As above, plus graft handling and technician time on hair restoration and laser consumables on ablative resurfacing. |

Circuit consumables — towels, laundry, water and amenities — are carried separately at $8 a visit across 2,345 monthly visits, or $18,760.

# Capital stack

| Scenario | Project | Private investment | SBA 7(a) loan | Stabilized DSCR |

| Ample · $1.5M private | $5,000,000 | $1,500,000 (30%) | $3,500,000 | 2.00x |

Debt service is interest-only for the first 18 months, then amortises over the remaining 102. Rate assumption is WSJ Prime 6.75% plus the 2.75% maximum spread permitted on 7(a) loans over $350,000.

The working capital and debt service reserve of $1,146,000 is **computed, not chosen** — it is sized against a modelled cash trough of $774,223 at month 14. That is why it is not a round number.
